capabilities: Import tafsīrs, ḥadīth, Qur'ān editions and dictionaries from online repositories
OCR scanned PDFs with Gemini and translate the transcriptions
Transliterate Arabic passages into Latin script
Annotate imported sources and keep annotations across re-renders
Export works to Zotero as book items
extras: Desktop only: runs local Python scripts and reads files outside the vault. Requires Obsidian 1.13 or later. Full guides are bundled in-app; an optional Zotero 7 companion plugin is installed separately. No telemetry; fonts are not downloaded.
motivation: Built for research on Islam and the Arabic language — Qurʾān commentaries, ḥadīth, the Qurʾān in its riwāyāt, and the classical dictionaries.
problem: Bringing a digitized Arabic text into Obsidian is manual work, and annotations, corrections and citations are easily lost when the source changes.

relations.evidence: Midad Arabic Sources’ ETA templating, managed-region merge, and note conventions follow ScholarWeft, which pioneered them.
Midad is optimized for integration with Zotero using the ScholarWeft Obsidian plugin
normally created by ScholarWeft or ZotLit; Midad does not create those notes

requires.name: Python 3 with PyMuPDF, requests and google-genai

summary: Imports classical Arabic texts into a vault and adds OCR transcription, transliteration, annotation and Zotero export.
